tools: One-line summaries: per-column count, mean, std and quartiles; counts per category; group averages; pairwise correlations.
The first twenty minutes with any new table; spotting missing values, skew, class balance and leaks.
Builds a full HTML report of a DataFrame: distributions, missing values, correlations, duplicates.
Wide tables where looking at every column by hand is too slow.
Statistical plots on top of matplotlib: histograms, scatter matrices coloured by class.
Seeing shapes that summaries hide (Anscombe's quartet).
Fills blanks with the column's mean, median, most frequent value or a constant, learned on training data; add_indicator=True adds 0/1 “was missing” columns.
The default way to handle missing values in a pipeline.
Fills each blank with the average of the k most similar rows (by distance on the other columns).
Missing values that other columns can predict (MAR); scale the columns first.
Model-based imputation: predicts each column with blanks from the others, round after round. Needs from sklearn.experimental import enable_iterative_imputer.
When columns are strongly related and accuracy of the fill matters.
Outputs 0/1 columns marking where values were missing.
When the fact that a value is missing carries signal.
Fast histogram-based gradient boosting that accepts NaN natively (learns which branch blanks go to) and can split on categories directly.
Tabular data with blanks and categories, with little preprocessing.
Scales each column as (x − median) ÷ IQR, so outliers don't set the scale.
Columns with outliers or heavy tails, before distance- or gradient-based models.
Linear regression with the Huber loss: squared for small errors, linear for large ones, so a few wild points can't take over.
Regression data with outliers you can't simply remove.
One 0/1 column per category; sparse by default; min_frequency / max_categories pool rare values; handle_unknown decides what unseen categories become.
Categorical columns with few to moderate distinct values.
One integer per category (alphabetical unless you pass categories=).
Real orders (S < M < L) and tree models.
Replaces each category by a smoothed mean of the target; fit_transform cross-fits (cv=5) so no row sees its own label.
Maps categories or tokens to a fixed number of columns with a hash function (default 2²⁰); no vocabulary stored.
Huge or open-ended vocabularies, streaming data.
Dozens of extra encoders (binary, James–Stein, leave-one-out, …) with the scikit-learn API.
Gradient boosting with built-in ordered target statistics for categorical features.
Scales each column to mean 0 and standard deviation 1, using statistics learned on training data.
Default scaler for kNN, SVMs, PCA, regularized and gradient-descent models.
Maps each column to [0, 1] with (x − min) ÷ (max − min).
When a fixed range is needed and there are no big outliers.
Reshape skewed columns toward uniform or Gaussian distributions.
Heavily skewed features for models that like symmetric inputs.
Adds powers and pairwise products of columns; interaction_only=True keeps just the products.
Giving linear models interactions and curves.
Smooth piecewise-polynomial features of a column; extrapolation="periodic" for cyclical values like hours.
Letting a linear model bend smoothly; time-of-day effects.
Wraps any function (date parts, ratios, logs) as a transformer so it can live in a pipeline.
Custom feature engineering inside a Pipeline.
Deep Feature Synthesis: builds aggregate and transform features across related tables automatically.
Relational data (customers, orders, items) with many possible aggregates.
Chains transformers and a final model into one estimator; fit fits each step on training data in order, predict replays them.
Always: leak-proof cross-validation and one object to deploy.
Applies different transformers to different columns and stacks the results; unlisted columns follow remainder (default "drop").
Tables with mixed types: numbers, small and large categories, dates, IDs.
Selects columns by dtype or name pattern, e.g. all numeric columns.
Pipelines that should adapt to new columns of a known type.
Makes transformers and pipelines return DataFrames with column names (dense output only).
Lists the output columns of a fitted transformer or pipeline, prefixed by step names.
Checking what the model actually sees; catching silently dropped columns.
Saves and loads a fitted pipeline to a file; only load files you trust.
Shipping the trained pipeline to production.
acronyms: Looking at the data with summaries and plots before modelling, to find surprises and problems.
Blanks are pure bad luck, unrelated to any value: dropping rows is unbiased (just wasteful).
Whether a value is missing depends on other columns you have; model-based imputation can fix the bias.
Whether a value is missing depends on the missing value itself (high earners hide income); only partly fixable, so keep an indicator.
The floating-point marker for a missing value; NaN is not equal to itself, so test with isna().
Q3 − Q1, the spread of the middle half of the data; used by the outlier rule and RobustScaler.
How well scores rank positives above negatives: 0.5 = random, 1.0 = perfect.
Split the training data into k folds; each fold is scored by a model trained on the others.
Predicts from the k closest training rows; distances make it sensitive to feature scales.
The typical size of a prediction miss, in the target's units.
terms: Numbers that squash a column: mean, median, standard deviation, quartiles, correlation. Different data can share them (Anscombe's quartet, Datasaurus).
How the target's classes are split (50/50 or 99/1); it sets the majority baseline and the right metrics.
The accuracy of always predicting the most common class; every model must beat it.
A feature that contains information about the label that won't exist at prediction time (recorded after the outcome).
A long tail on one side of a distribution; the mean is pulled away from the median.
Filling missing values with a guess learned from training data (mean, median, neighbours, a model).
A 0/1 column marking where a value was missing, so the model can use missingness as a signal.
Dropping every row that has any blank; unbiased only when data is MCAR, and wasteful with many columns.
A value far from the rest: either an error to fix or a real rare case to keep (sometimes the very thing you predict).
(x − mean) ÷ std: how many standard deviations a value is from the mean; |z| > 3 is a common outlier flag.
Several outliers inflating the mean and std so much that none of them looks extreme by z-score.
Not dragged around by a few extreme values (median, IQR, Huber loss).
The number of distinct values in a categorical column; it decides the encoder.
One integer per category; implies an order and distances.
Mapping categories to a fixed number of columns with a hash function; collisions are the price.
Replacing a category by the (smoothed) mean target of its rows; leaks unless computed out-of-fold.
Blending a category's mean with the global mean, weighted by its count: (n·mean + m·global) ÷ (n + m).
Computing each training row's encoding from the other folds only, so no row sees its own label.
CatBoost's leak-free target encoding: each row uses only rows before it in a random order.
A small learned vector per category, trained by a neural network.
Putting features on comparable scales so no column dominates distances, penalties or gradients.
Transforming a column to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
Building new columns from existing ones with domain knowledge: ratios, differences, date parts, interactions, aggregates, text counts.
Representing wrap-around values (hours, weekdays) as sin and cos of their angle, so 23:00 and 00:00 are neighbours.
A product of two features (“this matters more when that is true”).
A history feature computed only from rows before the prediction moment, never including the current label.
Features computed differently in training and in production, so the model sees different inputs live.
One estimator made of preprocessing steps and a final model, refitted as a unit inside cross-validation.
What a ColumnTransformer does with columns not listed: "drop" (default) or "passthrough".
